post.caption: California's state gem was mistaken for sapphire. Blue crystals turned up in California's San Benito County, and a prospector reportedly thought they were sapphire. Berkeley's George Louderback identified it as a new mineral in 1907 and named it benitoite, after the San Benito region. Most benitoite is violetish blue, and pink stones are very rare. In some directions its fire exceeds a diamond's, and under short-wave ultraviolet light it glows bright blue. California made benitoite its state gem in 1985, and San Benito County is the only commercial source of gem-quality benitoite. Most cut benitoite weighs less than one carat.
